coaching.headline: Four favored lanes and a won fight count (5-4) — lost 2-7 on towers, because Neon cashed everything and we cashed almost nothing.
coaching.team: This loss was not the lanes: mid, offlane, jungle and support all read favored, and we won more fights than they did (5 to 4). It was the exchange rate. We cashed 2 of our 5 won fights (the 14.9, 19.2 and 26-minute wins bought nothing); they cashed 2 of 4 and every fight we lost carried a price tag — Bayle's 15.9 pickoff became their Fangtooth at 16.2, the 21.9 loss became their tower at 22.4, and the two end-game dives became the tower chain that ended it. Those two dives were the same mistake taken twice: all five of us pushed past their towers, 1-5 at their inner tower at 23.5 and 2-5 at their inhibitor at 28.3, into a fed Neon. The modeled item counts say we were AHEAD in both fights (14-8, then 15-9) — the gold was fine, the call was not. Objectives ended 9-24. Up four lanes, make them walk to us; don't hand a fed midlaner defense fights on their side of the map.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: Two five-man dives past their towers into a 16-kill Neon: 1-5 at their inner tower (23.5, which bought them both inner towers at 23.9 and 24.2) and 2-5 at their inhibitor (28.3, followed by our inhibitor at 29.2 and the core at 29.6). By the modeled item counts we led both fights 14-8 and 15-9 — these were lost on the decision, not the builds.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31's seven deaths on Bayle were the tempo leak: caught alone at 12 by Neon and at 15.9 by Argus — the second directly cost Fangtooth at 16.2 — then down in both the 23.5 and 28.3 dives that ended it. The warding was genuinely good (9 wards); the routes were the problem. With a fed Neon on the map, the jungler crosses the river with company or not at all.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 carried the only unfavored lane to a team-best 10/5/6 with 30763 damage on Legion, including a solo 2-0 at their outer tower at 14.9 — a fight they answered by taking Fangtooth across the map, the trade the whole team kept accepting. The deaths that mattered: 21.9 (their tower fell at 22.4) and 28.8 (inhibitor 29.2, core 29.6). At 28 minutes the fed carry is the last body into a fight at their inhibitor, not part of a 2-5.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster won the resource game on Shinbi — 32001 mitigated on a 0/3/6 line — but was across the map, alive and ahead, when the 10.4 fight at our Fangtooth was lost 1-4; the macro read says a shove-and-rotate there flips the numbers. Being ahead in a side lane is only worth something when the lead walks to the fight.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim beat Neon in lane start to finish — the mid verdict reads ours all game — and that same Neon finished 16/5/2 because the kills came outside the lane: Gadget was caught alone by Neon at 25.4 and again at 29.5, and the 25.4 death turned the next fight into a 4v5 (won 2-1 anyway, to the team's credit). Winning the lane only counts if the mid stops being the enemy carry's gold source after laning ends.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs had a live game on Steel (5/5/7, favored lane all game) bookended badly: the 3.9 catch by Sparrow early, and the 29.0 death right before the inhibitor (29.2) and core (29.6) fell. The build also drifted fully off the winning core — Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves were all missing — and against a Phase heal comp with a Serath dive threat flagged before the game, the peel items are the fight.

threats: Heal-stacking: Phase. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback), Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

Stack (Kept alive in fights): 4 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Overseer, Noxia, Aion. Together they made staying in a long fight cheaper: more armor, shields or healing the longer it went.

Stack (Every ability hit set off): 3 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Wraith Leggings, Noxia. Neon has 4 damaging abilities (Erase Vector, L.I.N.X, Data Burst hit an area, so one cast sets them off on several heroes), and 63 ability haste brought them back 39% sooner: more casts, more triggers.
Stack (Damage that scales with the target's health): 2 effects on one trigger: Megacosm, Noxia. The more health a target stacks, the more these deal, so health items on the other side fed them.
The Eternal was part of it: Aion (Bottomless Vial + Runic Focus) sits on the same trigger as the items (kept alive in fights), so the same hits paid out twice.

Countered? 3 of the 5 players Neon killed built magical armor (Steel, Legion, Shinbi). Anti-heal on Legion, Shinbi. Health items on Steel, Shinbi raised the %-health damage they took. We killed Neon 5 times.
Copy it? Aion (Bottomless Vial + Runic Focus): 47.4% in 420 Neon midlane games, level with the hero's 47.7%. A standard setup: what made it work was this game, not a secret build.

loadout.text: Replace your trinket with Dox, granting you 5% increased Magical Power & 15% increased Maximum Mana. Activating it allows you to see nearby Enemy Heroes within 3000u for 4s.
loadout.plain: Swaps her trinket for one that reveals nearby enemy heroes, plus extra magic power and mana. Good for scouting before diving with Erase Vector.

loadout.name: Aion
loadout.text: Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.
loadout.plain: Each cast adds mana regen and ability damage to heroes earns gold. Neon casts constantly to build Threads, so this keeps her mana and gold flowing.

loadout.name: Bottomless Vial
loadout.text: Killing a River Buff restores a Potion charge and grants +5 Magical Power permanently.
loadout.plain: Taking a river buff refills a potion and grants permanent magic power. A jungle or roaming habit, not tied to her abilities.

loadout.name: Runic Focus
loadout.text: Gain 0.2% increased Magical Power per 1% current Mana.
loadout.plain: More magic power while Neon's mana bar is high. Rewards poking from full mana instead of spending it all at once.

loadout.name: Epoch
loadout.text: Stasis Device:  Enter Stasis for 2.5s.
loadout.plain: Freezes Neon in place, untouchable, for a moment. Use it when divers jump on Neon to waste their combo and wait for allies to help.

loadout.name: Press the Advantage
loadout.text: Upon achieving a Takedown, a Rally Point is spawned at the dead Targets location. Rally Point no longer grants Health Regeneration but increases Legions Rate of Fire by 14/18/22/26/30% and grants Allies 10/12.5/15/17.5/20% Attack Speed.

ability.name: Rally Point
ability.what: Legion calls in a standard and becomes Unstoppable for 0.5s, dealing 20/25/30/35/40 (+20%) Physical Damage whilst Knocking Back nearby Enemies.

loadout.plain: Every takedown drops a free Rally Point where the enemy died. It stops healing but speeds up your rifle and your team's attacks, so one kill in a teamfight snowballs into the next.

loadout.name: Thraex
loadout.text: Mark the last Enemy Hero damaged by your Basic Attack for 3s, increasing your damage against them by 3% (+0.4% per level) and reducing the damage they deal to you by 1.5% (+0.35% per level).
loadout.plain: Rifle shots mark the hero you hit: you deal more to them and take less from them. Best when you lock onto one target and keep shooting instead of swapping.

loadout.name: Alpha's Court
loadout.text: Deal 6% bonus damage when no allied hero is within 800 units.
loadout.plain: Bonus damage only while no ally hero is close by. Fits a solo lane or split-pushing, not standing with your team in fights.

loadout.name: Rallying Roar
loadout.text: Gain 10 Ultimate Haste. Casting your Ultimate grants you and allies within 1500 units 25% Movement Speed for 4s. 20s cooldown.
loadout.plain: Orbital Sanction comes back sooner, and casting it gives you and nearby allies a burst of speed to chase or reposition while the beam tracks targets.

loadout.name: Pacifier
loadout.text: Adrenalize:  Dash a short distance. Empower your next Physical Damage Instance within 3s. Deals 30 (+25%) Damage. Increased by 2.5x against Targets below 20% Max Health. Killing a Hero within 3s allows Adrenalize to be recast for 6s.
loadout.plain: Dash in, and your next physical hit, a rifle shot or Frag Order, deals extra damage, much more against nearly dead heroes. A kill lets you recast it to chase the next one.
